title: Design: a Lead Technician message pushes the fields below it down
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design picture "card-02-n1-rest.png" (board 1.2) attached to this case is open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced; it has one approved labor line and one part, and its one "Sales Representative" field reads {Sales-rep-A}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in that browser window.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Without any message showing, measure the gaps between Lead Technician, Service Advisor and Sales Representative.
  2. Make the Lead Technician message show.
  3. Look where the message sits and measure the gaps below it.
  4. Make the message go away and measure the gaps again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: every gap is 16 px, as in the picture of board 1.2.
  • Step 2: a message shows directly below the Lead Technician field.
  • Step 3: the message sits directly under Lead Technician and pushes Service Advisor and the Sales Representative field down; nothing overlaps.
  • Step 4: every gap is 16 px again.

Step 2 cannot be carried out yet: no source says what makes a Lead Technician message show. The case stays on hold until the product owner answers (question Q-C).

From: Chris Ward's answers, question sheet of 19 Oct 2026, Google Sheet 17Ry1BtRTPEkecBP5TlgAE0T93Ai1TQewdJ7B7WpWDBQ, tab "Questions for Chris", rows 6-43 (answered 19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026
